name: LightClaw
vibe_summary: A single-binary Rust rewrite of the OpenClaw concept, shipping agentic tooling, memory, and Telegram/Discord integration in a ~15MB executable. It positions itself as the fast, local-first, low-footprint alternative for users who want Claw without the heavy runtime.
best_for: Users wanting a single-binary, low-footprint AI assistant
Raspberry Pi / ARM and low-resource device deployments
avoid_if: You need a mature plugin ecosystem or web dashboard
You require Windows as a first-class platform
You want battle-tested sandboxing around shell tools
openclaw_advantages: ~15MB single binary vs heavy multi-component install
Near-instant startup and low memory footprint
Broad platform support including ARMv7 and Raspberry Pi
Local SQLite memory with no external vector DB
openclaw_disadvantages: Smaller community and ecosystem than OpenClaw
Windows support is unstable and second-class
Fewer integrations and no full control UI
Younger codebase with less security hardening history

overview_markdown:
LightClaw is a Rust-based, single-binary reimagining of OpenClaw, inspired by both OpenClaw and HKUDS's nanobot. It packages an agentic assistant — with file, shell, web, and scheduling tools — into a ~15MB executable with no Python runtime or heavy dependencies, targeting near-instant startup and a minimal memory footprint. It is powered by the Rig framework and supports OpenClaw-style `SKILL.md` skills via an `activate_skill` mechanism.

The project ships a local-first memory system built on SQLite: per-session short-term history, periodic summarization of conversation chunks, and semantic retrieval over stored memories, all without an external vector database. It integrates natively with Telegram and Discord via high-performance polling, supports multiple LLM providers (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Ollama, Mistral) with model fallbacks, and recently added XDG base directory support and ARMv7 builds for devices like older ARM boards and e-readers.

Compared to OpenClaw, LightClaw trades ecosystem breadth and UI surface for deployability and footprint: one binary, one config file, and broad platform coverage (Linux x86_64/ARM64/ARMv7, macOS Intel/Apple Silicon, with Windows present but less stable). Recent commits show active maintenance — rebranding from femtobot, shell-guard fixes, and firecrawl configuration — suggesting a young but moving project best suited to self-hosters who value simplicity over feature depth.
